n| `--compose-skill <id...>` | No | Project-shared skill IDs to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-secret <id...>` | No | P
roject secret IDs the composed stack grants to its runs (`secrets list` shows them) |\n| `--save-targets` | No | Attach the compos
ed environments to the suite (append, capped at 10). Without it the stack is ephemeral |\n\n#### Composing a target instead of nam

ing one

`--compose-client <id-or-name>` builds an execution stack for this run instead of
naming a saved environment, refined
by `--compose-computer`, `--compose-model`,\n`--compose-server-group`, `--compose-skill` and `--compose-secret`. The stack becomes
an unnamed,\ncontent-addressed environment (the same one `environments ensure-adhoc`\nproduces), so composing the same stack twic

e reuses one environment.
`--compose-host` is the deprecated spelling of the same flag.

`--compose-model` and `--compose-secre
t` carry the deployment requirement\ndescribed under [Deployment support for model overrides and secret\ngrants](#deployment-suppo
rt-for-model-overrides-and-secret-grants): a launch that names\neither is refused before it composes anything if this deployment d

oes not
publish the capability.

> [!WARNING]
`--wait` it exits **4** (see the exit-code table above). A per-target failure
d

oes not abort its siblings, so exiting 0 would let a pipeline read "1 of 3
runs never started" as a clean launch.

#### `--fi

le`: upload and run a suite file

`eval run --file` reads the versioned suite file (`schemaVersion: "1"`),
authenticates, the
n validates. A contract-invalid file exits **2** after the\nauth request — it does not start a run. `eval validate` on the same by

tes
still exits 1: that command is a verdict on the file; this one is not.

The file's `suite.id` is the declared suite identit
y. The first run creates a\nfile-owned suite stamped with that id; later runs of the same id in the same\nproject update that suit
e rather than creating a second one. A UI-authored\nsuite has no declared id, so no file can claim it. Resolve is never by name.\n
\nFile `passThreshold` is a fraction; the hosted suite grades on a percent. The\nconversion refuses rather than approximates. A fi
le count above **10**\n(`repetitions` in a `schemaVersion: \"1\"` file, `iterations` in `\"2\"`) is\nrefused by name (`REPETITIONS

_CAP`) and is not clamped.

**Which vocabulary the sync speaks is the deployment's call.** Before writing
anything, the CLI rea
ds `GET /capabilities` once. A deployment that advertises\n`vocabulary.version: 2` gets every request with `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabula
ry: 2`\nand case bodies spelled canonically — `iterations` (the exact count),\n`legacyIterations` (the legacy floor, the same numb
er) and `assertions` —\ninstead of `repetitions` / `iterations` / `checks`. A deployment without the\ncapability block, or without
the capabilities route at all, is spoken to in\nvocabulary 1, byte-for-byte as before. Nothing in the file changes either way:\nt
he dialect of the file and the vocabulary of the wire are independent.\n\nCases are synced in batches of at most 100 (`create_eval
_cases`). Every\ndeclared case is created or updated, including `disabled: true` rows. A case\nthe file **no longer declares** is
deleted from the hosted suite before\nlaunch. A case the file still declares but marks `disabled: true` is **kept,\nwith its histo
ry** — it is simply left out of the launch, so parking a flaky\ntest does not destroy its past results and re-enabling it later re

sumes the
same case.
The run is scoped to the enabled cases either way. A file with no enabled
cases is refused (`NO_ENABLED_CA
SES`) rather than launching the whole\npersisted suite. `--case` may only name an enabled case. A later run updates\nexisting case
s by declared id and creates new ones. An enabled case that\noverrides `passThreshold` is refused: hosted grading is suite-wide. A

disabled case with the same override is ignored, matching how repetitions
are checked. Authored
`defaults.toolPolicy` and non-
empty `defaults.validity` gates are refused at\nhosted CLI launch (`TOOL_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED` / the corresponding validity\nrefusal
). Hosted platform-authored suites do not currently have a backend\ntool-policy field or enforcement path, so the CLI does not upl
oad a suite that\nwould claim those guarantees. When supported by an eval runner, `toolPolicy`\nis enforced at execution time with
denied tools kept visible but blocked;\nserver annotations are advisory and **UNTRUSTED**. The file's default count\n(`defaults.r
epetitions`, or `defaults.iterations` in `schemaVersion: \"2\"`) is\ninherited per case and is not uploaded as a suite `minIterati
ons` floor.\nAuthored `defaults.systemPrompt` and `defaults.temperature` are uploaded as\nexecution defaults; omitted fields stay
omitted so the platform applies its\nown defaults. `target.hosts` and `target.environment` are attached before\nlaunch. A file env
ironment takes precedence over file hosts for that launch,\nwhile an explicit CLI target takes precedence over both. When an expli
cit CLI\ntarget is provided (for example `--host`), the file's `target.hosts` are\n**not** synchronized to the suite's persisted h
ost attachments — the suite\nkeeps whatever hosts it already has. Host attachment synchronization only\nruns when no explicit CLI

target overrides the file. Environment attachment
synchronization is unaffected and always runs.

Without `--idempotency-key`,
the CLI mints a fresh UUID for every invocation\nand prints it to stderr before launch (`Eval idempotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvo
cation therefore starts and bills a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse was lost — without starting a second run — pass the
key that was\nprinted: `--idempotency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `deduped` in\nthe receipt and human output. `--notes

` is not part of the key.

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-run approval

Every file run performs the same
live check `eval validate --project` performs,\n**before it writes anything**. It is not opt-in and there is no flag to skip\nit.

A file with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no
round trip.

What happens when a deterministic refer

ence does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Selected (enabled, and named by `--case` if you us
ed it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced** — nothing is written and nothing is billed |\n| Imported, not selected
| Its claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still persisted**, so the hosted record says what M
CPJam found rather than still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, not selected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-
written case never acquires an `import` block from this — \"somebody wrote this\" and \"something converted this\" are different f

acts |

Each target is checked on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked against
that host's configured servers rather tha
n the file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects — validating `target.servers` would approve a tool the host\ncannot reach.
A host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are attached to the host before launch) and the
host's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\nis a real, empty set — it clears the attachm
ent before launch — and is\nvalidated as such, never as an omitted field. A step that pins `serverId` is resolved by id;\n`serverN

ame` is a display fallback and never overrides it.

If the run's target set cannot be enumerated before the suite exists
(`--al
l-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pins a server the project no longer has, the launch

refuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hosted row id, which does not exist yet when this ch
eck\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore treated as possibly naming\nany enabled case, so an unresolved reference

still refuses; the launcher
resolves the selector itself a moment later.

A selected `approximated` case refuses unless this in

vocation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--allow-approximated <case...>` | No | Approve an `a
pproximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHORED case id (`cases[].id`). Repeatable. `--file` runs only |\n| `--appro
